beats.intent: A rectangle with sides x + 3 across and x + 2 down, split into four parts
beats.narration: Draw a rectangle x plus three wide and x plus two tall, split where x meets the numbers.
beats.code:
stage.title("Expanding (x + 3)(x + 2)")
xs, xw = 2.0, 1.2
A = Rectangle(width=xs, height=xs, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
B = Rectangle(width=xw * 1.5, height=xs, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(A, RIGHT, buff=0)
Cc = Rectangle(width=xs, height=xw, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(A, DOWN, buff=0)
D = Rectangle(width=xw * 1.5, height=xw, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(B, DOWN, buff=0)
parts = VGroup(A, B, Cc, D).move_to(ORIGIN)
stage.play(FadeIn(parts))
stage.add(parts)
stage.label(A, "x", direction=UP)
stage.label(B, "3", direction=UP)
stage.label(A, "x", direction=LEFT)
stage.label(Cc, "2", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: Each part labelled with its area: x^2, 3x, 2x, 6
beats.narration: The four pieces have areas x squared, three x, two x and six.
beats.code:
for r, t in ((A, "x^2"), (B, "3x"), (Cc, "2x"), (D, "6")):
    stage.play(FadeIn(MathTex(t, font_size=36).move_to(r)), run_time=0.3)

beats.intent: The rectangle beside (x + 3)(x + 2) = x^2 + 5x + 6
beats.narration: Add them: x squared plus five x plus six. Read backwards, that is how you factorise.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"(x + 3)(x + 2) = x^2 + 5x + 6")

request: why does x^2 = 9 have two answers?

beats.intent: Axes with the parabola y = x^2
beats.narration: Here is y equals x squared.
beats.code:
stage.title("Two square roots")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-4, 4), y_range=(0, 12))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: x ** 2)

beats.intent: A horizontal line at y = 9 crossing the parabola twice
beats.narration: Draw the line y equals nine. It crosses the parabola twice.
beats.code: line = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(-4, 9), ax.c2p(4, 9), color=YELLOW, dashed=True)

beats.intent: The crossings at x = -3 and x = 3 marked beside x = ±3
beats.narration: At three and at minus three, because minus three squared is also nine.
beats.code:
a = mark_point(stage, ax, -3, 9, color=RED, label="x = -3")
b = mark_point(stage, ax, 3, 9, color=RED, label="x = 3")
stage.equation(r"x^2 = 9 \Rightarrow x = \pm 3")

beats.intent: A box labelled ×2 then +1, with the input 3 arriving from the left
beats.narration: A function is a machine: put a number in, follow the rule, get a number out. Put in three.
beats.code:
stage.title("A function machine")
m1 = VGroup(Square(side_length=1.3, color=BLUE), Text("×2", font_size=30)).shift(LEFT * 1.2)
m2 = VGroup(Square(side_length=1.3, color=GREEN), Text("+1", font_size=30)).shift(RIGHT * 1.2)
stage.play(FadeIn(m1), FadeIn(m2))
stage.add(m1, m2)
x = Text("3", font_size=40, color=YELLOW).move_to(LEFT * 4.5)
stage.play(FadeIn(x))
stage.add(x)

beats.intent: The number moving through: 3 becomes 6, then 7
beats.narration: Times two makes six, plus one makes seven.
beats.code:
stage.play(x.animate.move_to(m1), run_time=0.8)
six = Text("6", font_size=40, color=YELLOW).move_to(m1)
stage.play(Transform(x, six))
stage.play(x.animate.move_to(m2), run_time=0.8)
stage.play(Transform(x, Text("7", font_size=40, color=YELLOW).move_to(m2)))
stage.play(x.animate.move_to(RIGHT * 4.5), run_time=0.8)

beats.intent: The machines beside f(x) = 2x + 1, f(3) = 7
beats.narration: The whole machine is f of x equals two x plus one, and f of three is seven.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"f(x) = 2x + 1,\quad f(3) = 7")

request: how do you undo a function, 2x + 1?

beats.intent: The machines ×2 then +1, with 7 at the output on the right
beats.narration: The function doubled and added one, turning three into seven. To go back, start from seven.
beats.code:
stage.title("The inverse function")
m1 = VGroup(Square(side_length=1.3, color=BLUE), Text("×2", font_size=30)).shift(LEFT * 1.2)
m2 = VGroup(Square(side_length=1.3, color=GREEN), Text("+1", font_size=30)).shift(RIGHT * 1.2)
stage.play(FadeIn(m1), FadeIn(m2))
stage.add(m1, m2)
y = Text("7", font_size=40, color=YELLOW).move_to(RIGHT * 4.5)
stage.play(FadeIn(y))
stage.add(y)

beats.intent: The machines flipped to −1 then ÷2, run right to left, turning 7 into 3
beats.narration: Undo the steps in reverse order: take one away, then halve. Seven becomes six, then three.
beats.code:
stage.play(Transform(m2[1], Text("-1", font_size=30).move_to(m2)), Transform(m1[1], Text("÷2", font_size=30).move_to(m1)))
stage.play(y.animate.move_to(m2), run_time=0.8)
stage.play(Transform(y, Text("6", font_size=40, color=YELLOW).move_to(m2)))
stage.play(y.animate.move_to(m1), run_time=0.8)
stage.play(Transform(y, Text("3", font_size=40, color=YELLOW).move_to(m1)))
stage.play(y.animate.move_to(LEFT * 4.5), run_time=0.8)

beats.intent: The machines beside f^{-1}(x) = (x - 1)/2
beats.narration: The inverse is x minus one, over two.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 1}{2}")

request: why is the square root of a negative number not allowed?

beats.intent: Axes with y = √x drawn from 0 to 9
beats.narration: The square root curve starts at zero and goes to the right.
beats.code:
stage.title("Where √x lives")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-5, 9), y_range=(0, 3.5))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, np.sqrt, x_range=(0, 9), label="\\sqrt{x}")

beats.intent: The region x < 0 shaded grey as outside the domain
beats.narration: Left of zero there is nothing: no real number squares to a negative.
beats.code:
bad = Rectangle(width=ax.c2p(0, 0)[0] - ax.c2p(-5, 0)[0], height=ax.c2p(0, 3.5)[1] - ax.c2p(0, 0)[1], color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0).move_to(ax.c2p(-2.5, 1.75))
stage.play(FadeIn(bad))
stage.add(bad)
stage.label(bad, "no real √", direction=UP, color=GREY_B)

beats.intent: The curve beside the domain x ≥ 0
beats.narration: So the domain of the square root is x greater than or equal to zero.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\sqrt{x}\ \text{is defined for}\ x \geq 0")

beats.intent: Bars doubling: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32
beats.narration: Keep doubling from two: four, eight, sixteen, thirty two.
beats.code:
stage.title("Solving 2^x = 32")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [2, 4, 8, 16, 32], labels=["2^1", "2^2", "2^3", "2^4", "2^5"])

beats.intent: The fifth bar, 32, lit
beats.narration: Thirty two is the fifth one.
beats.code: highlight(stage, bars[4], color=RED)

beats.intent: The bars beside 2^5 = 32, x = 5
beats.narration: So two to the fifth is thirty two, and x is five.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"2^x = 32 = 2^5 \Rightarrow x = 5")

request: how does the quadratic formula find the roots of x^2 - 2x - 3?

beats.intent: Axes with the parabola y = x^2 - 2x - 3
beats.narration: Here is x squared minus two x minus three.
beats.code:
stage.title("The quadratic formula")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-3, 5), y_range=(-5, 6))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: x ** 2 - 2 * x - 3)

beats.intent: The formula with a = 1, b = -2, c = -3 substituted beside the graph
beats.narration: Put a equals one, b minus two, c minus three into the formula.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{16}}{2}")

beats.intent: The roots x = 3 and x = -1 marked where the curve crosses the axis
beats.narration: The root of sixteen is four, so x is three or minus one: exactly where the curve crosses the axis.
beats.code:
r1 = mark_point(stage, ax, 3, 0, color=RED, label="3", direction=DOWN)
r2 = mark_point(stage, ax, -1, 0, color=RED, label="-1", direction=DOWN)
